is_anopheles.evidence: Female An. funestus collected throughout Uganda and western Kenya... (Page 1, Abstract)

reports_target_markers.evidence: The L119F-GSTe2 mutation was recently shown to play a major role in the DDT resistance in West Africa [27]. To assess the role of this mutation in the DDT resistance in Uganda a Taqman assay [27] was used to genotype 30 mosquitoes dead after 1 h exposure to 4% DDT (susceptible) and 30 mosquitoes alive (resistant) from Jinja. (Page 3, Role of the L119F-GSTe2 mutation in the DDT resistance in Uganda)

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: 30 mosquitoes dead after 1 h exposure to 4% DDT (susceptible) and 30 mosquitoes alive (resistant) from Jinja were genotyped for L119F-GSTe2 (Page 3). Genotyping detected the 119F allele at 10% frequency, with 73.3% of resistant mosquitoes being L119/L119 homozygotes (Page 5, Figure 6B and 6C).

african_field_population.evidence: Adult Anopheles mosquitoes were collected from six districts in Uganda (Bulambuli, Lira, Masindi, Jinja, Arua, Tororo) and Kisumu-Siaya in West Kenya between December 2011 and June 2012 (Page 2, Study sites / Mosquito collections).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical study reporting field collections, WHO bioassays, molecular species ID, Plasmodium infection rates, qRT-PCR expression analysis, and GSTe2/VGSC genotyping.

sub_country_location.evidence: Specific districts and coordinates provided: Bulambuli (1°10'N, 34°23'E), Lira (2°14'N, 32°54'E), Masindi (1°40'N, 31°42'E), Jinja (0°26'N, 33°12'E), Arua (3°1'N, 30°54'E), Tororo (0°41'N, 34°10'E) in Uganda and Kisumu-Siaya (0°05'S, 34°15'E) in Kenya (Page 2, Study sites).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquito collections were carried out between December 2011 and June 2012 (Page 2, Mosquito collections).

duplicate_risk.evidence: New primary field collections carried out between Dec 2011 and June 2012 specifically for this study.

supplement.evidence: All relevant genotype data for L119F-GSTe2 (30 dead and 30 alive mosquitoes from Jinja, genotype frequencies) are detailed in the main text and Figure 6.

assessment.summary: This study reports widespread pyrethroid and DDT resistance in Anopheles funestus across 6 districts in Uganda and western Kenya. Target-site mutation analysis confirmed absence of kdr mutations (L1014F/S) in VGSC, while metabolic resistance via cytochrome P450s is the main driver. The GSTe2 L119F mutation was genotyped in 60 mosquitoes (30 DDT-resistant and 30 DDT-susceptible) from Jinja, Uganda, showing low allele frequency (10%) but a significant association with DDT resistance.
